title: OSCAL4Rail Change Impact Constraints (additive over the NIST OSCAL Mapping Model)
description: Standalone constraint schema for an OSCAL4Rail Change Impact report. The report IS an OSCAL artifact: a NIST OSCAL 'mapping-collection' that maps a source catalog version to a target catalog version; this schema checks the railway/governance-specific conventions on top of (not instead of) the NIST OSCAL Mapping schema, run as a second validation pass. Rationale (ADR-019): the whole framework keeps governance machine- and agent-readable with Code as the single source of truth; the change must therefore stay an OSCAL artifact under the OSCAL4Rail schema (a Governance-as-Code object, i.e. the rule catalog), not a free report. One OSCAL mapping is both the human-readable report and the agent-readable diff, and it is the artifact L4 re-assessment consumes (the L1+L2 -> L3 -> L4 circle). The OSCAL4Rail change semantics ride on the native map/@relationship (qualified by an O4R namespace) plus O4R props; no foreign fields are invented (OSCAL-native, no fork, ADR-016/018). This schema deliberately does NOT $ref the NIST schema (Variant A, two-pass). See docs/reference/change-format.md and ADR-019.

version.description: Version of this change report (a derived artifact; not the compared catalogs' versions, which are the mapping's source/target resources).

oscal-version.description: The pinned OSCAL version the report is produced under (SSOT, ADR-008).

mappings.description: At least one mapping from a source catalog state to a target catalog state.

o4r-change-mapping.description: A NIST mapping between two versions of the same rule catalog. source-resource = old state, target-resource = new state (ADR-014 version coupling). Each 'map' is one control-level change.

props.description: Mapping-level O4R props. MUST declare the O4R change namespace marker so a consumer can recognise this as an OSCAL4Rail change report.

source-gap-summary.description: Controls present in the SOURCE (old) only: removed controls (ADR-019, NIST gap-summary). A removed control has no target, so it cannot be a map.

target-gap-summary.description: Controls present in the TARGET (new) only: added controls. An added control has no source, so it cannot be a map.

existence-gap.description: A NIST gap-summary listing controls that exist on only one side (added or removed). Keeps existence changes OSCAL-native and upgradeable, instead of an invalid one-sided map.

versioned-resource.description: A NIST mapping-resource-reference to a compared catalog state, carrying its version via an O4R prop so the version coupling (ADR-014) is explicit in the report.

o4r-change-map.description: One control-level change, expressed as a NIST 'map'. The change category rides on @relationship qualified by the O4R namespace; the old/new signal snapshot and the impact chain ride on O4R props.

ns.description: MUST be the OSCAL4Rail change namespace, so @relationship is read as an O4R change category, not a generic NIST relationship.

relationship.description: The governance-primary change category for a two-sided change (change-format.md section 4.1). Existence changes (added/removed) are NOT relationships; they are expressed via the NIST source-/target-gap-summary, because a NIST map requires both sources and targets.

sources.description: The control in the OLD state (mapping-item type=control, id-ref=control-id). A map always has both sides; one-sided existence changes use the gap-summary instead.

targets.description: The control in the NEW state. A map always has both sides; one-sided existence changes use the gap-summary instead.

props.description: O4R change props: old/new signal snapshot, superseded-by, and the impact chain.

control-item.description: A NIST mapping-item referencing a control by its stable control-id.

name.description: O4R change prop names: dimension, old-modality, new-modality, old-rank, new-rank, old-polarity, new-polarity, old-lifecycle, new-lifecycle, superseded-by, affected-context, affected-cascade, required-action, secondary-category.
